newsitem.title: MALTA: Malta's Lombard Bank profit up.
newsitem.headline: Malta's Lombard Bank profit up.

text.p: Lombard Bank (Malta) said it had posted a pre-tax profit of 335,000 Malta pounds ($875,087) for the six months ending on March 31, up 34 percent on the corresponding period last year.

The bank said the improved performance was the result of a rise of 35 percent in operating income and 18 percent in net interest receivable, which outweighed an 18 percent increase in operating expenses.

Bank chairman Albert Muscat told a stockbrokers' meeting on Wednesday evening that over 30 percent of operating revenues were derived from non-interest income, confirming progress in the bank's efforts to diversify its revenue base.
Muscat said the net interest margin was down to 26 percent, reflecting the presence of large foreign currency placements from offshore customers which are redeposited on a conservative basis.
Deposits in Maltese currency have gone up by 25 percent, while loans and advances to customers were up by 35 percent over March last year, Muscat said.

With shareholders' funds of Lm3.76 million, the net asset value per share works out at Lm1.25. Earnings have expanded by 1c per share to 7c per share. The board has not declared an interim dividend. ($1: 0.38c3 Malta pounds)
